blocks.text: We can increase the flow velocity of water in a rubber pipe by squeezing it. When we squeeze the rubber pipe, we decrease the cross-sectional area through which the water flows. According to the equation of continuity,

where A is the cross-sectional area and v is the flow velocity. By decreasing the cross-sectional area (A₂ < A₁), the velocity of the water (v₂) must increase to maintain the same flow rate. Therefore, squeezing the rubber pipe increases the flow velocity of water.
